A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASL/AMP perceptron-sampling work despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original empirical stability distributions for spherical perceptrons in Figure 4 and cross-entropy sampling success rates over 100 runs in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the spherical experiments and reports new log-potential sampling experiments and MCMC comparisons in Figures 2, 3, and 6–8.

M1.justification: v1's exploratory cross-entropy target measures are replaced by a constraint-enforcing log-potential target for binary perceptrons. v2 also introduces a distinct sampling procedure: Metropolis-Hastings with an annealed, piecewise potential U_tau(s) approaching -log(s) (Section 4.4.2).

E1.justification: Both versions study synthetic random spherical and binary perceptron problems. Gaussian inputs already appear in v1 Appendix A.2, alongside binary inputs elsewhere. The new potentials and algorithms retain this task coverage; structured-data applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 introduces direct algorithmic comparisons against standard temperature-annealed MCMC with potential U(s)=-sΘ(-s), evaluated against the proposed tau-annealing scheme in Figure 3 and Appendix E.3. v1 contains no corresponding MCMC baseline comparison.

E3.justification: New MCMC protocols use 100, 200, or N sweeps and system sizes up to 8192. Log-potential ASL experiments use T=0.5 and N=1000, 2000, 5000, and 8000, replacing cross-entropy experiments with beta=10, gamma=2 and different sizes. The retained spherical stability experiment keeps its original settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds a binary log-potential stability-distribution check against theory (Figure 2), plus analyses of MCMC sensitivity to sweep budgets and system size, including N-scaled budgets and inverse-size plots (Appendix E.3). The spherical stability validation is retained.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 5 specifies means and standard deviations over 100 runs. v2 Figure 6 reports averages over 250 simulations but does not define its displayed error bars; MCMC uncertainty details are also unspecified. These concern different experiments, so the counts do not establish increased repetitions of a retained experiment.

E6.justification: The cross-entropy success curves are removed and new log-potential results accompany a predicted ASL threshold near alpha=0.65. MCMC results support a tau-annealing threshold near 0.55 with N sweeps. These are new results under different conditions, not same-setting gains. The reported spherical frontier is also revised to fall slightly short of d1RSB.

T1.justification: v2 adds an asymptotic analysis near q=1 explaining the obstruction for non-diverging potentials and deriving the log-potential condition T<1 (Appendix F). It generalizes replica and stability-distribution calculations to arbitrary potentials and adds reference-system and saddle-point equations, replacing the cross-entropy-specific derivations.

C1.justification: v1 leaves efficient constraint-enforcing binary sampling for future work. v2 claims a controlled log-potential sampler and an effective tau-annealed MCMC procedure. Its spherical-sampling claim is narrowed from the entire replica-symmetric region to most of that region.

C2.justification: v2 explains binary sampling failure through the persistent q=1 peak and how a diverging potential removes it. It adds qualifications concerning reference-system replica symmetry, AMP failure on correlated or structured data, and strong finite-size effects with a possible RSB-related threshold gap (Section 3 and Appendix E.2.2).

D1.justification: v2 specifies root-finding for the spherical-prior norm multiplier and explains when channel integrals are analytic. New MCMC schedules are documented. Conversely, v1's explicit outer Euler-Maruyama pseudocode is omitted in favor of a general description of SDE discretization.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions its formalism beyond Ghio et al.'s planted setting and its binary sampler relative to heuristic solvers. It substantially expands cited discussion of diffusion–MCMC hybrids, other ASL applications, and perceptron geometry and hardness; the cross-entropy positioning around Baldassi et al. (2020) is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds an explicit contribution list and fuller Bayesian and sampling-failure explanations, and reorganizes the appendices around a general derivation followed by model-specific applications and limiting analysis.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 1–2 are consolidated into v2 Figure 1 with a transition-detail inset. The uniform-binary plots move to appendix Figure 5, and new log-potential and MCMC displays are added. The side-by-side main-text algorithms become one full-width appendix algorithm, alongside substantial title and page-layout restyling.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves efficient constraint-enforcing binary sampling unresolved. v2 substantially addresses this gap with a theoretically motivated log potential, empirical stability checks, and an MCMC construction tested against a temperature-annealing baseline and varying budgets. It also narrows the spherical claim to match the reported transition. These gains outweigh weaker error-bar documentation and the remaining limits of finite-size and MCMC distributional validation.
